mechanism_fidelity.rationale: Repeated comparable queue and elapsed-time measurements produce temporal patterns evaluated against expected variation and explicit change rules. Those patterns constrain whether accumulation persists, worsens or resolves. The mapping preserves the source's limits concerning measurement error, regression to the mean, sampling, changing conditions and intervening actions.

target_fidelity.rationale: Handoff-specific elapsed times, pending-case ages and flow imbalance directly support locating observed delay accumulation. Ownership records nominate a bounded assignment change, and the pilot evaluates whether retaining it is supported within the tested scope. This is an explicitly bounded contribution to both parts of the target question.

operational_coherence.rationale: The specified observations can produce the stated temporal signals, which warrant the limited descriptive and pilot-retention inferences. The mapping distinguishes candidate mechanisms from established causes, checks downstream and quality outcomes, and requires inconclusive findings when comparisons or sample sizes are inadequate. Provisional durations and thresholds do not independently warrant success.

validity.rationale: The proposed protocol preserves serial monitoring's mechanism, addresses the retained question and bounds its conclusions to what comparable observations can support. Its untested status leaves empirical outcomes unknown without invalidating the mapping.

uncertainty: Ticket timestamp availability, meanings and reliability have not been demonstrated; the protocol explicitly requires verification and limits interpretation when approval-start data are absent.
Adequate case counts, monitoring duration and suitable thresholds remain unknown; the protocol allows an inconclusive result rather than assuming adequacy.
No evidence establishes actual delay locations, an ownership-related cause or benefit from automatic assignment.
